title: Foraging
summary: Foraging can help in a crisis, but safe identification and conservative choices are essential.

sections.heading: Step 1 — Prioritize calories and safety
sections.body: In a survival situation, calories, water, and safety matter more than variety. Focus on easy-to-identify, non-toxic foods first, and conserve energy while gathering them. A small amount of safe food is better than risking poisoning by eating an unknown plant.
sections.image_description: A survival kit next to simple safe foods like roots, fruits, and nuts.

sections.heading: Step 2 — Identify plants with confidence
sections.body: Use multiple identification features such as leaf shape, stems, flowers, fruit, habitat, and season. Never rely on one feature alone because many plants look alike. If you cannot identify a plant with high confidence, leave it alone.
sections.warning: If you are unsure, do not eat it. 'Maybe edible' is not safe in a survival setting.
sections.image_description: A plant identification checklist showing leaves, flowers, stems, and habitat.

sections.heading: Step 3 — Avoid universal danger plants and risky mushrooms
sections.body: Some plants and fungi are dangerous even in small amounts, and many mushrooms are deadly or cause delayed poisoning. Avoid mushrooms unless you have expert-level identification skills and local knowledge. Plants with milky sap, bitter almonds smell, or unknown berries should also be treated with extreme caution.
sections.image_description: A red warning symbol beside a cluster of wild mushrooms and unknown berries.

sections.heading: Step 4 — Understand the universal edibility test limits
sections.body: The universal edibility test is often discussed, but it is slow, uncomfortable, and not reliable enough to make dangerous plants safe. It may have a place in extreme emergencies after many better options are exhausted, but it is not a guarantee. Your best protection is positive identification from trusted local knowledge or a reputable field guide.
sections.warning: Do not use the universal edibility test on mushrooms or obviously toxic plants.
sections.image_description: A caution sign over a step-by-step test chart with a large question mark.

when_to_use: Use this guide when other food sources are limited and you need to gather wild plant foods carefully.
do_not: Do not taste-test unrecognized plants casually.
Do not over-prioritize low-calorie foods when safer calories are available.
sources: IFRC / Red Cross wilderness first aid guidance, 2021
